About Kamboh Technologies

# A software company in Lahore, engineering with purpose.

Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited is a software engineering company based in Johar Town, Lahore, Pakistan. We design and build mobile apps, web platforms and custom business software for companies at home and abroad.

Meet the Team Our Services

Based in Pakistan
Clients at home and abroad
Mobile, web and custom software
Support after launch

Who we are

## A product team for businesses that want software done properly.

We work the way good product teams work. We learn how your business runs, agree on what success looks like, then ship in small, visible steps, so you always know where your project stands and what comes next.

Our work covers the whole journey: shaping the idea, designing the experience, building the mobile and web apps, connecting the systems behind them, and keeping everything running once real users arrive.

Reliable products Software that keeps working after launch day, with tests, monitoring and clean code.

Plain communication Regular demos and updates in language your whole team understands.

Built to grow Architecture that leaves room for new features, users and markets.

Why Kamboh

## The principles behind every project.

How we work matters as much as what we build. These six principles shape every decision, from the first workshop to the last release.

### Modern technologies

We choose proven, well-supported tools such as Flutter, Next.js and PostgreSQL, so your product is easy to maintain and easy to hire for.

### Business-focused solutions

Features are prioritised by the value they bring to your business. We will tell you when something is not worth building yet.

### Clean architecture

Clear structure, code reviews and documentation mean another developer could open the codebase and understand it quickly.

### Scalable applications

We plan data models and infrastructure for the growth you expect, without over-building for traffic you don't have yet.

### Thoughtful user experience

Interfaces are designed around real tasks and checked with real users, so people can use your product without a training manual.

### Collaborative development

You get regular demos, a shared project board and direct contact with the people building your product.

What happens next

## From first message to kickoff.

No long sales process. Four simple steps, and you decide at each one whether to continue.

- We read your inquiry Someone who builds software reviews it, not a sales script, and replies with any questions.

- A short discovery call We talk through your goals, users, timeline and budget, and suggest the simplest way to get there.

- Scope and estimate You receive a written scope with priorities, assumptions and an estimate you can compare.

- Kickoff Once you're happy, we set up the project board and start with discovery and design.

Why Kamboh

## Engineering Excellence at Every Step.

How we work matters as much as what we build. These are the principles behind every project we take on.

### Which technologies do you use?

We choose proven, well-supported tools such as Flutter, Next.js and PostgreSQL, so your product is easy to maintain and easy to hire for.

### How do you decide what to build first?

Features are prioritised by the value they bring to your business. We will tell you when something is not worth building yet.

### Will other developers be able to work on our code?

Clear structure, code reviews and documentation mean another developer could open the codebase and understand it quickly.

### Can our app grow as our business grows?

We plan data models and infrastructure for the growth you expect, without over-building for traffic you don't have yet.

### How do you make software easy to use?

Interfaces are designed around real tasks and checked with real users, so people can use your product without a training manual.

### How will we stay involved during the project?

You get regular demos, a shared project board and direct contact with the people building your product.

## Six things that shape your estimate.

Want the details? Read our guide to what affects the cost of building an app .

01

### Features and complexity

The number of screens, user roles and features, and how complex each one is.

02

### Platforms

Web, iPhone, Android or all three. Cross-platform tools like Flutter keep this efficient.

03

### Design

From a clean standard interface to fully custom design with prototypes and user testing.

04

### Integrations

Payments, maps, SMS, ERPs and other services each need to be connected and tested.

05

### Timeline

Faster delivery may need a bigger team working in parallel.

06

### Support after launch

Updates, monitoring and new features once real users are on board.

Pricing questions

## Frequently asked questions.

### Why don't you publish fixed prices?

Every business needs something different, and a price without a clear scope is usually wrong. After a short discovery call, we send a written scope with priorities, assumptions and an estimate, so you know exactly what you are paying for.

### How do I get an estimate?

Send us a few details through the contact form or WhatsApp. We reply with questions, have a short discovery call about your goals, users, timeline and budget, then send a written scope and estimate.

### Can we start small and add features later?

Yes, and we usually recommend it. Launching a focused first version gets you to market sooner, keeps the first budget lower and lets real users show you what to build next.

### How are payments structured?

Most projects start with an advance payment, with the balance due on agreed milestones and before final handover. The exact schedule is written in your proposal. See our contract information for details.

### Do you work with clients outside Pakistan?

Yes. Clients in Pakistan are usually invoiced in Pakistani rupees and international clients in US dollars or another agreed currency, with regular video calls and updates around your time zone.

### Are there costs besides your fee?

Third-party costs such as hosting, domains, app store accounts, paid APIs and government fees for SECP or FBR filings are separate. We list them clearly in your estimate.

Web platform

## Business Management Platform

One dashboard for sales, stock and staff across several branches, so owners see the whole business without chasing reports.

The problem Each branch keeps its own spreadsheets, so owners wait days for numbers and decisions are made on outdated data.

Key features
- Live sales, stock and staff figures per branch

- Low-stock alerts and transfer requests

- Role-based access for owners, managers and staff

- Exportable daily and monthly reports

Stack
- Next.js

- PostgreSQL

- REST APIs

Plan a project like this

Example concept

Mobile app

## Mobile Commerce Application

A shopping app with catalogue search, cart, wallet and card payments, and live order tracking from checkout to doorstep.

The problem Customers order by phone or chat, orders get lost, and there is no easy way to reorder or track a delivery.

Key features
- Fast catalogue search with filters

- Cart, wallet and card payments

- Live order status with push notifications

- One-tap reorder from order history

Stack
- Flutter

- Dart

- Firebase

Plan a project like this

Custom software

## Custom CRM Solution

A lead pipeline with follow-up reminders, contact history and team reports, built around how your sales team already sells.

The problem Leads arrive from several channels, follow-ups depend on memory, and managers can't see which deals are stuck.

Key features
- Drag-and-drop pipeline stages

- Automatic follow-up reminders

- Full contact and conversation history

- Team performance reports

Stack
- React

- Node.js

- Supabase

Web and mobile

## Digital Service Platform

Online booking and payments for a service business, plus a staff app that keeps appointments, reminders and schedules in sync.

The problem Bookings come in by phone, double-bookings happen, and customers forget appointments.

Key features
- Online booking with live availability

- Deposits and payments at checkout

- Automatic reminders before each appointment

- Staff app with daily schedules

Stack
- Next.js

Ask Kamboh AI

### How do you estimate a project?

We start with a short discovery call, then write a scope document that lists features, priorities and assumptions. The estimate is based on that scope, so you can see exactly what is included.

### Do you work with clients outside Pakistan?

Yes. We work with businesses at home and abroad, with regular video calls, a shared project board and updates scheduled around your time zone.

### Who owns the code and designs?

Ownership is set out in the project agreement. In a typical client project, the code, designs and documentation are handed over to you at the end of the engagement.

### Can you take over an existing app?

Yes. We begin with a code review to understand the current state, list the risks and quick wins, then agree on a plan to stabilise and improve the product.

### What happens after launch?

We monitor the product, fix issues and keep dependencies up to date. Many clients continue with a support plan or a dedicated team to keep improving the product.

Overview

## What we deliver.

Starting a company in Pakistan means dealing with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). We handle the paperwork for you: checking and reserving your company name, preparing the incorporation documents and filing them online.

Once the company is incorporated, we help you register it for an NTN with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and explain the yearly compliance filings, so your business starts on the right footing.

- Founders registering a new private limited company

Title: AI Agents for Small Business: A Practical 2026 Guide
Summary: What AI agents are, where they save small businesses time, what they cost to run, the risks to manage and a 30-day plan to launch your first one.

Home Blog AI & Automation
AI & Automation

# AI Agents for Small Businesses: A Practical Guide for 2026

By the Kamboh Technologies team 4 November 2026 11 min read

A couple of years ago, “using AI” mostly meant typing a question into a chat window. In 2026 the conversation has moved on to AI agents : software that can understand a request, decide what to do, use your business tools and complete a task, with a person approving the steps that matter.

For a small business that is a real opportunity. An agent can answer customers at midnight, read a stack of invoices or follow up with every lead, so a small team can serve more people without burning out. It is also an area full of hype. This guide separates the two: what agents are, where they pay off, what they cost, the risks to manage, and a realistic 30-day plan to launch your first one.

Key takeaways

- An AI agent is a language model plus your knowledge, your tools and clear rules . The model is the easy part; the rules and integrations are the real work.

- Start with one repetitive, high-volume process , such as answering common questions or qualifying leads, not your whole business.

- Keep a person in the loop for anything involving money, commitments or sensitive data.

- Measure hours saved and response times from day one, so you know whether it is actually working.

## What is an AI agent, in plain language?

Think of an agent as a new team member with four parts:

- A brain: a large language model (LLM) that understands requests written in normal language and works out what to do next.

- Knowledge: your own information, such as services, prices, policies, FAQs and product specs, so its answers are about your business and not the internet in general.

- Tools: actions it is allowed to take, such as checking an order, creating a lead in your CRM, booking a meeting or drafting an email.

- Guardrails: rules about what it must never do, when to ask for confirmation and when to hand over to a human.

A real example: the Ask Kamboh AI assistant on this website answers questions about our services in English, Urdu or Roman Urdu. When a visitor is ready to start a project, it collects their details, reads them back for confirmation , and only then fills in the contact form or sends the inquiry to our team. That confirmation step is a guardrail, and it is what makes the agent safe to put in front of customers.

## Chatbot vs automation vs AI agent

These three terms are often mixed up. The difference matters, because each suits a different job:

Feature Rule-based chatbot Workflow automation AI agent

How it works Fixed menus and scripted replies “When X happens, do Y” steps Understands the request and decides which steps and tools to use

Best for Simple, predictable menus Repetitive tasks that never change Varied requests written in everyday language

Weak spot Breaks when people go off-script Cannot handle exceptions or judgement Can make mistakes, so it needs guardrails and review

In practice the best systems combine them: an agent understands the customer, then triggers a reliable, rule-based workflow to do the actual update.

## Seven high-value uses for a small business

### 1. Customer support on WhatsApp and your website

Most small businesses answer the same twenty questions every day: prices, timings, delivery, location, order status. An agent can answer them instantly, at any hour, in the language the customer writes in, and pass the conversation to a person when it gets complicated.

### 2. Lead qualification and booking

Instead of a form that sits unanswered, an agent can ask a prospect a few smart questions (what they need, their budget range, their timeline), log a clean summary in your CRM and suggest a meeting time. Your sales team starts every call already knowing the context.

### 3. Invoices, receipts and documents

Agents are very good at reading documents. They can pull supplier names, amounts, dates and tax figures from invoices or purchase orders into a spreadsheet or accounting system, and flag anything that does not match, leaving your accountant to review instead of retype.

### 4. Sales follow-ups and quotations

An agent can draft follow-up emails after a meeting, prepare a first version of a quotation from your price list, or remind a customer about a pending payment. A person reviews and sends, so nothing goes out without approval.

### 5. An internal knowledge assistant

New staff ask the same questions about policies, procedures and product details. An internal assistant that answers from your own documents (and shows where the answer came from) saves senior staff hours every week and makes onboarding faster.

### 6. Reports and summaries

Connected to your POS, ERP or spreadsheets, an agent can send a short daily summary: yesterday's sales, top products, unusual spikes, overdue invoices. Owners get the picture without opening five dashboards.

### 7. Content and catalogue work

Product descriptions, social posts, translations and catalogue updates are ideal first drafts for an agent. Keep a person in charge of the final version, especially for prices, claims and brand tone.

## Where an AI agent is the wrong tool

Good advice includes knowing when not to use AI. Avoid agents, or keep them strictly in an advisory role, when:

- The decision is high-stakes and irreversible , such as approving refunds, loans or legal and tax positions, without human review.

- The process itself is broken. Automating a messy process only produces mess faster. Fix the process first.

- There is no reliable information to work from. If your prices and policies are not written down anywhere, the agent has nothing trustworthy to answer from.

- The volume is tiny. If a task happens twice a month, a checklist is cheaper than an agent.

## What it costs to run an AI agent

Costs come in four parts, and it helps to budget for each separately:

- Setup and integration. Writing the instructions, organising your knowledge, connecting your tools (CRM, WhatsApp, email, ERP) and testing. This is usually the largest one-off cost.

- Model usage. Most AI providers charge per amount of text processed. For a small business answering customer questions this is often modest, but it grows with volume and with long documents.

- Channel and platform fees. Some channels charge separately. The WhatsApp Business Platform, for example, has its own messaging charges set by Meta.

- Monitoring and improvement. Reviewing conversations, updating knowledge when prices change and improving answers. Plan a few hours a month.

Practical ways to keep running costs low: use a smaller, faster model for simple questions, keep answers short, limit how much history is sent with each message, and send only the documents a task needs. We use these same techniques on our own assistant.

## The risks, and how to manage them

### Confident but wrong answers

Language models can produce answers that sound right but are not, often called “hallucinations”. Reduce this by limiting the agent to your own knowledge, telling it to say “I'm not sure” and hand over when it does not know, and showing a short notice that AI answers are confirmed by your team.

### Privacy and data protection

Only send the agent the data it needs. Check your AI provider's data terms, in particular whether your content can be used to train or improve their models, and choose a plan that excludes it where possible. In Pakistan, the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (amended in 2025) already applies to how data and information systems are handled, and a dedicated personal data protection law has been proposed but not yet enacted. If you serve customers in Europe, the GDPR applies too. Tell customers when they are talking to an AI and link to your privacy policy.

### Actions without approval

Give the agent the smallest set of permissions it needs. It can draft a refund, but a person approves it. It can collect a customer's details, but confirms them before submitting. Log every action so you can see what happened and why.

### Manipulation through messages or documents

People can try to trick an agent with instructions hidden in a message or a file (“ignore your rules and…”). This is known as prompt injection. Treat everything from outside your business as untrusted, never give the agent access to secrets it does not need, and test it with attempts to break the rules before launch.

## A 30-day plan to launch your first agent

- Week 1: choose and measure. Pick one process with high volume and clear answers. Record the baseline: how many requests, how long each takes and how fast you reply today.

- Week 2: gather knowledge and write the rules. Collect your FAQs, prices and policies in one place. Decide what the agent may do, what needs approval and when it hands over. Write 30 real customer questions to test with.

- Week 3: build the pilot. Connect the agent to one channel and one tool. Test it with your team, including deliberately difficult and off-topic questions, and fix the gaps.

- Week 4: launch small and review. Open it to real customers, read the conversations every day for the first week, update its knowledge and compare the results with your baseline.

## How to tell whether it is working

Track a handful of numbers rather than relying on impressions:

- Resolution rate: the share of conversations solved without a person.

- Hand-over rate and reasons: what the agent could not handle, which tells you what to teach it next.

- Response time: how quickly customers get a useful first reply.

- Leads and conversions: whether more inquiries turn into meetings and sales.

- Hours saved: time your team gets back each week, multiplied by its cost, minus the agent's running costs.

## Checklist before you build

- One clearly defined process and a measured baseline

- Up-to-date written knowledge: services, prices, policies, FAQs

- A list of actions the agent may take, and which need approval

- A clear hand-over path to a real person

- An AI provider and plan whose data terms you have checked

- An updated privacy policy and an “AI assistant” notice for customers

- Someone responsible for reviewing conversations every week

## The bottom line

AI agents are not magic and they are not a replacement for a good team. Used well, they take over the repetitive, round-the-clock work, so your people can focus on customers, quality and growth. Start with one process, keep a person in control of what matters, measure the results and expand from there.

If you would like help choosing the right first use case, or building an agent connected to your website, WhatsApp or business systems, our team in Lahore can map it out with you.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a lot of data to use an AI agent?

No. Most small-business agents work from information you already have: your services, prices, policies and common questions. What matters is that this information is accurate, up to date and written down in one place.

### Can an AI agent reply in Urdu and Roman Urdu?

Yes. Modern language models handle English, Urdu and Roman Urdu well, and can reply in the language the customer uses. Always test with real customer messages, because spelling and mixed-language styles vary a lot.

### Will an AI agent replace my staff?

For most small businesses, no. An agent takes over repetitive questions and data entry so your team can spend more time on sales, service and work that needs judgement. A person should stay in charge of anything involving money or commitments.

### Is my business data safe with an AI agent?

It can be, if it is set up carefully: send only the data a task needs, choose an AI plan whose terms exclude using your data for training where possible, restrict the agent's permissions and keep access logs. Avoid putting passwords, card details or sensitive personal data into an agent.

### How long does it take to build an AI agent?

A focused pilot for one process, such as answering website questions or qualifying leads, can often be live in a few weeks. Agents connected to several systems, such as an ERP, CRM and WhatsApp, take longer because each integration needs building and testing.

Technology

# Flutter vs React Native: Which Should Your Business Choose?

By the Kamboh Technologies team 4 November 2026 6 min read

In short

- Flutter (by Google) and React Native (by Meta) both let one codebase power apps for iPhone and Android, and both are proven in production.

- Flutter draws its own interface, so apps look the same on every device. React Native uses each platform's native components and suits teams that already work in JavaScript and React.

- Both perform well for typical business apps; the experience of the team matters more than the framework.

- Kamboh Technologies uses Flutter as its default for new cross-platform apps, but the right choice depends on your product and team.

If you are planning a mobile app, you will probably hear two names: Flutter and React Native . Both let a team build one app that runs on iPhone and Android, which saves time and money compared with building two separate native apps. So which one is right for your business? Here is a plain-language comparison.

## What they have in common

- One codebase for iOS and Android

- Large communities and long-term support from major companies (Google for Flutter, Meta for React Native)

- Used in production by well-known apps around the world

- Fast development with live reload, so changes appear instantly while building

Either can produce an excellent app. The differences are in the details.

## Design and consistency

Flutter draws its own interface, so your app looks the same on every device and every operating system version. That makes it a strong choice for brand-focused designs, custom animations and pixel-perfect layouts.

React Native uses the phone's native interface components. Apps feel very native to each platform, but small visual differences between iOS and Android are more common.

## Performance

For most business apps, such as shopping, booking, delivery or dashboards, both perform very well. Flutter compiles to native code and is known for smooth animations. React Native has improved its performance significantly with its newer architecture. In practice, good engineering matters more than the framework.

## Development speed

Both are fast. Flutter comes with a complete set of ready-made interface components, so teams often move quickly on design-heavy apps. React Native benefits from the huge JavaScript ecosystem, which is helpful if your team already builds websites with React.

## Hiring and long-term maintenance

This is often the deciding factor. React Native uses JavaScript, one of the most widely known programming languages. Flutter uses Dart, which is easy to learn and has a fast-growing developer community. Ask yourself who will maintain the app in two or three years, and choose a framework your team, or your development partner, knows well.

## Quick comparison

- Choose Flutter if you want a highly consistent, brand-driven design, smooth animations and one team owning the whole app.

- Choose React Native if your team already works with React on the web and wants to share knowledge and code between the website and the app.

## What we recommend

At Kamboh Technologies, Flutter is our default for new cross-platform apps because one codebase delivers a consistent, native-quality experience on both platforms and keeps maintenance simple. That said, the best choice depends on your product, your team and your plans. A good development partner should explain the trade-offs for your specific case rather than pushing one answer for everyone.

## The bottom line

Both Flutter and React Native are excellent, proven choices. Focus on your product's needs, your long-term maintenance plan and the experience of the team building it. Get those right, and either framework can power a successful app.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which is better for a business app, Flutter or React Native?

Both are excellent, proven choices. Flutter gives a very consistent look on every device from one codebase, while React Native is a natural fit for teams already strong in JavaScript and React. The best choice depends on your product, your team and your maintenance plans.

### Is Flutter faster than React Native?

For most business apps, both are fast enough that users will not notice a difference. Performance depends far more on how well the app is built than on which of the two frameworks is used.

### Can one codebase really run on both iPhone and Android?

Yes. That is the main benefit of both Flutter and React Native. One codebase is built into apps for both platforms, which usually reduces development time and long-term maintenance.

### Which framework does Kamboh Technologies use?

Flutter is our default for new cross-platform apps, because one codebase delivers a consistent, native-quality experience on both platforms and keeps maintenance simple. We still recommend what fits each project best.

Home Blog Business Setup
Business Setup

# How to Register a Private Limited Company with the SECP: Step-by-Step Guide

By the Kamboh Technologies team 4 November 2026 7 min read

In short

- To register a private limited company in Pakistan, you apply online to the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) .

- The main steps are: choose the company type, reserve the company name, prepare the documents and director details, file the incorporation application, and receive the certificate of incorporation.

- After incorporation, register the company with the FBR for a National Tax Number (NTN).

- Registration is not the end: companies must file annual returns with the SECP and tax returns with the FBR every year.

Registering your business as a private limited company gives it a separate legal identity, makes it easier to open business bank accounts and sign contracts, and builds trust with clients. In Pakistan, companies are registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) under the Companies Act, 2017. Here is how the process works.

## Step 1: Choose the right company type

The two most common options for small and growing businesses are:

- Private limited company : at least two members and two directors. Suitable for partners or founders starting together.

- Single member company (SMC) : one person owns the company, with a nominee named in case something happens to the owner.

Both give limited liability, which means the owners' personal assets are generally protected from company debts.

## Step 2: Check and reserve your company name

Your company name must be available and acceptable under SECP rules. Names that are too similar to existing companies, misleading or restricted are usually not approved. Prepare two or three options so you have alternatives, and reserve the approved name through the SECP's online system.

## Step 3: Prepare your documents and information

Before filing, gather:

- CNICs (or passports for foreigners) of all directors and members

- Contact details, addresses and occupations of directors and members

- The registered office address of the company

- The main business activity (the principal line of business)

- The share capital and how shares are divided between members

The company's Memorandum of Association (what the company does) and Articles of Association (how it is run) are also prepared at this stage.

## Step 4: File for incorporation online

The incorporation application, together with the memorandum, articles and required details, is submitted online to the SECP along with the prescribed fee. The SECP reviews the application and may ask for corrections.

## Step 5: Receive your certificate of incorporation

Once approved, the SECP issues a certificate of incorporation with a Corporate Unique Identification Number (CUIN). Your company now legally exists. Certificates can be verified online through the SECP's verification service, which is useful when clients or banks want to confirm your registration.

## Step 6: Register for an NTN with the FBR

A newly incorporated company should register with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) for a National Tax Number (NTN). You will need the NTN to open a business bank account, issue proper invoices and file tax returns.

## Step 7: Stay compliant every year

Registration is the start, not the end. Companies have ongoing duties, including:

- Filing annual returns with the SECP

- Keeping proper books of account and company records

- Filing income tax returns with the FBR on time

- Reporting changes such as new directors or a new registered address

Missing these filings can lead to penalties, so it helps to keep a simple compliance calendar.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Choosing a name that is too similar to an existing company

- Using an incomplete registered office address

- Describing the business activity too vaguely

- Forgetting NTN registration and tax filing after incorporation

## Need help?

Company registration is straightforward once you know the steps, but the paperwork can be time-consuming. If you would rather focus on your business, Kamboh Technologies can prepare the documents, file with the SECP and register your NTN for you.

This article is general information, not legal advice. Requirements can change, so always check the latest rules with the SECP.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I register a company in Pakistan?

Apply online to the SECP: reserve a company name, prepare the incorporation documents (including the Memorandum and Articles of Association) and director details, file the incorporation application with the prescribed fee, and receive your certificate of incorporation. Then register with the FBR for an NTN.

### What is the difference between a private limited and a single member company?

Both are private companies registered with the SECP. A single member company has one shareholder and director, while a private limited company usually has two or more. Your choice depends on how many owners the business has and how you plan to grow.

### Do I need an NTN after registering my company?

Yes. A newly incorporated company should register with the Federal Board of Revenue for a National Tax Number. You need it to open a business bank account, issue proper invoices and file tax returns.

### How can someone verify that a company is registered with the SECP?

The SECP provides an online verification service where a company's registration details can be checked, which is useful when clients or banks want to confirm that a business is genuinely incorporated.

### What do companies have to do every year after registration?

File annual returns with the SECP, keep proper books of account and company records, file income tax returns with the FBR on time, and report changes such as new directors or a new registered address.

Title: Mobile App Development Cost in Pakistan: What Affects It
Summary: A practical guide to what drives the cost of building a mobile app in Pakistan: features, platforms, design, backend, integrations and maintenance.

Home Blog Mobile Apps
Mobile Apps

# What Affects the Cost of Building a Mobile App in Pakistan?

By the Kamboh Technologies team 4 November 2026 6 min read

In short

- The cost of a mobile app in Pakistan depends mainly on scope : how many features it has and how complex they are.

- Other big factors are one platform or two, the design, the backend and admin panel, integrations such as payments, testing and store approval, and maintenance after launch.

- A cross-platform framework such as Flutter usually lowers cost, because one codebase runs on both iPhone and Android.

- Launching a focused first version (an MVP) is the most reliable way to control cost and get to market sooner.

“How much will my app cost?” is the first question almost every business asks, and the honest answer is: it depends on what the app needs to do . Two apps that look similar on the surface can take very different amounts of work behind the scenes. This guide explains the main factors so you can plan a realistic budget and compare quotes fairly.

## 1. The number and complexity of features

Features are the biggest driver of cost. A simple information app with a few screens is very different from an app with user accounts, payments, live tracking and a chat system. Each feature needs design, development, testing and ongoing maintenance.

A useful exercise is to list every feature and mark it as must-have or nice-to-have . Launching with only the must-haves (often called an MVP, or minimum viable product) gets you to market faster and lets real users tell you what to build next.

## 2. One platform or two

Your customers probably use both iPhone and Android. Building two separate native apps means two codebases to build and maintain. A cross-platform framework such as Flutter lets one codebase run on both, which usually reduces build time and long-term maintenance without giving up a native look and feel.

## 3. Design and user experience

A polished, easy-to-use design is not decoration; it decides whether people keep using your app. Custom design, animations and a clickable prototype take time, but they also prevent expensive changes later because you test the idea before development starts.

## 4. The backend and admin panel

Most apps need more than the app itself. Behind the scenes there is usually:

- A database and API that store users, orders and content

- An admin panel where your team manages everything

- Notifications , file storage and security

Using a managed backend service can speed this up, while a custom backend gives more control. Either way, it is a real part of the project and should be in the quote.

## 5. Integrations with other services

Payment gateways, maps, SMS, courier tracking or your existing ERP each add work. Every integration needs to be connected, tested and handled gracefully when the other service is slow or unavailable.

## 6. Testing, launch and app store approval

Testing on different devices and screen sizes, fixing issues and preparing App Store and Google Play listings all take time. Apple in particular reviews every app, so store preparation should be part of the plan rather than an afterthought.

## 7. Maintenance after launch

An app is never truly “finished”. New iOS and Android versions, security updates, bug fixes and new features all need ongoing work. When comparing quotes, ask what support after launch looks like.

## How to get an accurate quote

The more clearly you describe your app, the more accurate the estimate. Before contacting any development team, prepare:

- A short description of the app and who it is for

- The three to five things users must be able to do

- Any apps you like as references

- Integrations you need, such as payments or maps

- Your ideal launch timeframe

A good team will then ask questions, suggest what to include in the first version and give you a written scope and estimate , so you know exactly what you are paying for.

## The bottom line

The cost of an app comes down to scope. Start with a focused first version, choose a cross-platform approach where it makes sense, and plan for maintenance from day one. That is how you launch sooner, spend wisely and grow the app based on real feedback.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to build a mobile app in Pakistan?

It depends on what the app needs to do. A simple app with a few screens costs far less than one with user accounts, payments, live tracking or chat. The most accurate way to know is to list your features, then ask for a written scope and estimate based on them.

### Is it cheaper to build one app for both iPhone and Android?

Usually, yes. A cross-platform framework such as Flutter uses one codebase for both platforms, which typically reduces build time and long-term maintenance compared with building two separate native apps.

### What is an MVP and why does it save money?

An MVP (minimum viable product) is a first version with only the must-have features. It gets you to market faster, costs less, and lets real users show you what to build next, instead of paying for features nobody uses.

### Do I need to budget for maintenance after launch?

Yes. New iOS and Android versions, security updates, bug fixes and new features all need ongoing work. Ask any development team what their support after launch looks like and include it in your budget.

### What should I prepare before asking for a quote?

A short description of the app and who it is for, the three to five things users must be able to do, any reference apps you like, the integrations you need, and your ideal launch timeframe.

# Accessibility Statement

We want everyone to be able to use our website, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, magnification or other assistive technologies. This statement explains what we do and how to tell us if something does not work for you.

Last updated 4 November 2026 3 min read Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

## Our commitment

Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited is committed to making kambohtechnologies.com accessible and usable for as many people as possible. We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at Level AA , the internationally recognised standard published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).

We also apply the same principles to the software we build for clients, because accessible products reach more customers and work better for everyone.

## Conformance status

We believe this website is partially conformant with WCAG 2.2 Level AA. “Partially conformant” means that most of the content meets the standard, but some parts may not yet fully do so. The known exceptions are listed below, and we are working on them.

## What we have built in

- Keyboard access: menus, the services dropdown, accordions, forms and the AI assistant can be used with a keyboard, with a clearly visible focus outline.

- Skip link: a “Skip to main content” link appears when you press Tab on any page.

- Structure: each page uses meaningful headings in order, landmarks (header, navigation, main content and footer) and breadcrumb navigation, so screen reader users can move around quickly.

- Text alternatives: informative images have descriptive alternative text; decorative images and animations are hidden from assistive technology.

- Colour and contrast: text and controls are designed to meet WCAG contrast ratios in both light and dark mode, and colour is never the only way information is shown.

- Forms: every field has a visible label; errors are explained in text, linked to the field and announced to screen readers.

- Reduced motion: if you turn on “reduce motion” in your device settings, we switch off smooth scrolling and decorative animations.

- Resizing and reflow: pages can be zoomed to 200% and viewed on small phone screens without losing content or needing to scroll sideways.

- Language: the page language is set so screen readers pronounce content correctly. Ask Kamboh AI can reply in English, Urdu or Roman Urdu.

- Light and dark themes: you can switch themes at any time from the header.

## Known limitations

- Embedded Google Map: the map on our Contact page is provided by Google and may not be fully accessible. The full address, phone number and a “Get directions” link are always available as plain text beside it.

- AI-generated replies: Ask Kamboh AI responses are generated automatically and their wording may sometimes be less clear than we would like. You can always contact our team directly instead.

- Visual project previews: some decorative illustrations of example projects are simplified visuals rather than real interfaces. Their meaning is described in the surrounding text.

- Third-party pages: links to external sites such as WhatsApp, Instagram, GitHub and government portals lead to content we do not control.

## How we test

We check the website with automated accessibility tools (such as Lighthouse and axe), by navigating pages with a keyboard only, at high zoom levels and on small mobile screens, and we are adding regular screen reader testing to this routine. We review accessibility whenever we add new pages or features, and we last reviewed this statement on the date shown above.

## Compatibility

The website is designed to work with recent versions of major browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari) on desktop and mobile, and with common assistive technologies such as NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and TalkBack. It may not work fully in older browsers.

## Feedback and help

If you have difficulty using any part of our website, or you need information in a different format, please tell us. We will do our best to help and to fix the problem.

- Email: info@kambohtechnologies.com (subject: “Accessibility”)

- Phone or WhatsApp: +92 302 8207226 , Monday to Friday, 6am to 10pm Pakistan time

Please tell us the page address, what you were trying to do and the problem you met, including the browser and assistive technology you use if possible. We aim to reply within 5 business days .

# Contract Information

Clear contracts make good projects. This page explains how our agreements are usually structured, so you know what to expect before we start. Your own signed agreement always sets the exact terms.

Last updated 4 November 2026 5 min read Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

## Our company details

Contracts and invoices are issued by our registered company. These details are useful for vendor registration and procurement:

Legal name Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

Company type Private limited company, incorporated in Pakistan

SECP CUIN 0297023

FBR NTN G813109

Office address Plot 111, Block A1, PIA Housing Society, Johar Town, Lahore 55030, Pakistan

Email info@kambohtechnologies.com

Phone +92 302 8207226 · +1 (416) 871-5643

Working hours Monday to Friday, 6am to 10pm (Pakistan time)

Copies of our certificate of incorporation and NTN certificate are available on request for vendor onboarding. You can also verify our registration on the SECP website, as explained on our About page .

## How an engagement works

- Discovery. We discuss your goals, users, features, timeline and budget, and ask questions until the scope is clear. If you need confidentiality from the first conversation, we are happy to sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) first.

- Proposal and quotation. We send a written proposal with the scope, deliverables, timeline, price and payment schedule. Unless it says otherwise, a quotation is valid for 30 days.

- Agreement. Work starts once the proposal or a service agreement (sometimes with a statement of work, or SOW) is accepted in writing by an authorised person and the first payment is received. Electronic signatures and written email acceptance are valid under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002.

- Delivery in milestones. Larger projects are split into milestones, such as design, development phases, testing and launch, each with clear deliverables you review and approve.

- Launch, handover and support. We deploy, hand over the agreed code, credentials and documentation, and provide the support described in your agreement.

## What your agreement covers

Every project agreement sets out, at a minimum:

- The scope of work and the deliverables, including what is not included

- The timeline and milestones, and what we need from you to keep to them

- The price, currency, payment schedule and taxes

- How changes to the scope are requested, priced and approved

- Ownership of the work, confidentiality and use of third-party components

- Acceptance testing, warranty, support and maintenance

- How either party can end the agreement, and how disputes are resolved

## Pricing models

Model How it works Best for

Fixed price An agreed price for a clearly defined scope, paid by milestone Projects with well-defined requirements

Time and materials You pay for the hours actually worked at agreed rates, with regular reports Evolving products and ongoing development

Monthly retainer A fixed monthly fee for an agreed amount of support, maintenance or growth work Maintenance, SEO and long-term partnerships

## Payments and invoicing

- Schedule: most projects start with an advance payment, with the balance due on agreed milestones and before final handover. The exact percentages are in your proposal.

- Currency: clients in Pakistan are usually invoiced in Pakistani rupees (PKR); international clients are usually invoiced in US dollars (USD) or another agreed currency.

- Invoices: issued by Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited with our NTN. Payment terms are stated on each invoice.

- Taxes: where applicable, provincial sales tax on services is charged in addition to our fees and shown separately, and withholding tax is handled as required by the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. Rates follow the law in force when the invoice is issued.

- Payment methods: bank transfer to our company account. We will never ask you to pay into a personal account; if you receive such a request, please call us to confirm.

- Third-party costs: hosting, domains, app store accounts, paid APIs, AI usage and government fees (for example SECP or FBR fees) are paid by the client, either directly or reimbursed at cost, and are listed separately.

## Change requests

New ideas often come up during a project, and that is normal. Any change to the agreed scope is described in writing with its impact on price and timeline, and is only carried out once you approve it. This keeps the budget predictable for both sides.

## Ownership of the work

- Once all payments for a deliverable are made, you own the custom code, designs and content we create specifically for you , and we transfer it to your accounts and repositories.

- We keep ownership of our pre-existing tools, libraries and know-how, and grant you a permanent licence to use any of them included in your product.

- Open-source components remain under their own licences, which we choose carefully so they are suitable for commercial use.

- Unless you ask us not to, we may mention that we worked with you and show non-confidential parts of the work in our portfolio.

## Confidentiality and data

We keep your business information, code and data confidential, and only share it with team members who need it for your project. We can sign your NDA or provide ours. Where we handle personal data on your behalf, we do so only on your instructions and can sign a data processing agreement. Read our Privacy Policy for how we handle personal information.

## Testing, acceptance and warranty

- Each milestone has an agreed review period. If you report issues, we fix anything that does not meet the agreed scope before it is accepted.

- After launch, a warranty period (stated in your agreement) covers fixing defects in our work at no extra cost.

- New features, changes in requirements and issues caused by third-party services, hosting or edits by others are outside the warranty and can be covered by a support plan.

## Support and maintenance

Software needs care after launch: security updates, operating system and browser changes, backups and monitoring. We offer optional monthly maintenance plans with agreed response times, so your product stays secure and up to date.

## SECP registration and tax filing services

For our SECP company registration and tax filing services, we prepare and submit documents based on the information you provide. You remain responsible for the accuracy and completeness of that information and for signing filings where the law requires it. Government fees are separate from our service fee, and approval timelines are decided by the relevant authority.

## Ending an agreement

Either party can end an agreement as set out in it, usually with written notice. If a project ends early, you pay for the work completed up to that point, and we hand over that work once it is paid for. Confidentiality and ownership terms continue after the agreement ends.

## Disputes and governing law

Our agreements are governed by the laws of Pakistan, including the Contract Act 1872. If a disagreement arises, both sides first try to resolve it through good-faith discussion between senior representatives. If that does not work, the agreement sets out the next step, which is usually arbitration or the courts at Lahore. International clients may agree a different arrangement in their contract.

## Questions before you sign?

We are happy to walk you through any part of our agreement or adapt it to your organisation's requirements. Email info@kambohtechnologies.com , call +92 302 8207226 , or send us your project details .

This page is a general summary of how our agreements usually work. It is not itself a contract; the terms of your signed agreement apply to your project.

# Cookie Policy

We keep cookies to a minimum. This page lists every cookie and browser storage item our website uses, what each one does and how long it lasts.

Last updated 4 November 2026 3 min read Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

The short version

- No advertising cookies and no cross-site tracking.

- Google Analytics cookies are set only after you click “Accept” .

- A few essential items remember your theme and your cookie choice.

Change cookie settings

## What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website saves in your browser. Similar technologies, such as local storage and session storage , let a website remember information on your device. In this policy, “cookies” covers all of these.

## Essential storage (always on)

These items are needed for the website to work as you expect. They do not track you and are never shared with anyone.

Name Type Purpose Duration

kt-theme Local storage Remembers whether you chose light or dark mode Until you clear your browser data

kt-consent Local storage Remembers whether you accepted or rejected analytics cookies, so we do not ask again on every page Until you change it or clear your browser data

kt-account Local storage Only if you sign in: remembers your first name so the navigation bar shows you are signed in Removed when you sign out or delete your account

firebaseLocalStorageDb IndexedDB (Firebase Authentication) Only if you sign in: keeps you signed in to your client account (or our team to the admin area) Until you sign out

kt-prefill Session storage Briefly holds details from Ask Kamboh AI when you ask it to fill in the contact form Deleted as soon as the form is filled, or when you close the tab

## Analytics cookies (only with your consent)

If you click “Accept”, we use Google Analytics 4 to understand how many people visit, which pages are useful and where we can improve. We use Google's Consent Mode, so these cookies are not set until you accept, and we do not use Analytics for advertising.

Name Provider Purpose Duration

_ga Google Distinguishes one visitor from another 2 years

_ga_<ID> Google Keeps track of your current visit (session) 2 years

Analytics data is kept for no longer than 14 months. Google's own use of this information is described in how Google uses information from sites that use its services .

## Third-party content

- Google Maps (Contact page): the embedded office map is provided by Google, which may set its own cookies when the map loads. You can use the “Get directions” link instead if you prefer.

- Google Fonts: our fonts are delivered by Google, which receives your IP address to send the font files. Google Fonts does not set cookies.

- Links to WhatsApp, Instagram and GitHub: these services set their own cookies only if you open them.

## Signed-in areas

If you sign in to a client account, or our team signs in to the private admin area, Firebase Authentication stores a secure sign-in session in the browser (listed above). Visitors who do not sign in never receive it.

## How to change your choice

You can accept or reject analytics cookies at any time using “Cookie settings” in the footer of every page, or the button at the top of this page. If you withdraw consent, analytics stops immediately. To remove cookies that were already set, clear the cookies for kambohtechnologies.com in your browser settings.

Most browsers also let you block or delete cookies entirely. Blocking essential storage may mean the website forgets your theme or asks for your cookie choice again.

## Changes and contact

If we add or change cookies, we will update this page and, where needed, ask for your consent again. For questions, email info@kambohtechnologies.com . For more about how we handle personal information, read our Privacy Policy .

- What cookies are

- Essential storage (always on)

# Disclaimer

Our website is designed to be helpful and accurate, but its content has limits. Please read this disclaimer before relying on anything you find here.

Last updated 4 November 2026 2 min read Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

## General information only

The content on kambohtechnologies.com, including our service pages, blog articles, guides and FAQs, is published for general information. It is not tailored to your circumstances and is not a substitute for professional advice.

## Not legal, tax or financial advice

Articles and pages about SECP company registration, tax filing, contracts or regulations explain processes in general terms. They are not legal, tax, accounting or financial advice . Laws, fees, deadlines and procedures in Pakistan and elsewhere change regularly. Before acting, confirm the current requirements with the relevant authority, such as the SECP or FBR, or a qualified professional. When you hire us for these services, the advice we give you is set out in our engagement with you.

## Ask Kamboh AI

Answers from our AI assistant are generated automatically by a third-party AI model. They can be incomplete, out of date or wrong, and they are not offers, quotes or commitments. Our team confirms every detail before any agreement.

## Prices, timelines and estimates

Any costs, timelines or estimates mentioned on the website or in articles are indicative and depend on the scope of each project. Only a written proposal from our team is binding.

## Examples and project previews

Some projects and interface previews on our website are concept examples created to illustrate the kind of work we do. Where this is the case, we describe them as examples. Results described for any project depend on many factors and are not a promise of similar results for your business.

## Reviews and testimonials

Any review cards marked “Sample” are layout placeholders, not real client reviews. We only publish genuine client feedback as real reviews, and we never pay for reviews. Individual experiences vary.

## External links and trademarks

Links to other websites are provided for convenience; we do not control or endorse their content. Names and logos of technologies, platforms and organisations mentioned on the website belong to their owners and are used only to describe our work. Their use does not imply any partnership or endorsement unless we say so.

## Accuracy and updates

We review our content regularly, but we cannot guarantee that everything is complete, current or free of errors at all times. If you spot something that is wrong or out of date, please tell us at info@kambohtechnologies.com and we will correct it.

## Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited is not liable for any loss or damage arising from reliance on the content of this website. Our full terms are in our Terms and Conditions .

# Privacy Policy

This policy explains what personal information we collect when you visit our website, chat with Ask Kamboh AI or work with us, why we collect it, who we share it with and the choices you have.

Last updated 4 November 2026 9 min read Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

Privacy at a glance

- We collect only what we need to answer your inquiry, deliver our services and keep the website secure.

- We do not sell your personal information , and we do not use advertising cookies.

- Analytics cookies are set only if you click “Accept” in the cookie banner. You can change your choice anytime.

- Ask Kamboh AI conversations are not stored in our database . Only an inquiry you ask the assistant to send is saved.

- If you create a client account, you can edit or delete it yourself at any time from your account .

- You can ask us to access, correct or delete your information by emailing info@kambohtechnologies.com .

## Who we are

This website, kambohtechnologies.com , is operated by Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited , a private limited company incorporated with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP CUIN 0297023, FBR NTN G813109), with its office at Plot 111, Block A1, PIA Housing Society, Johar Town, Lahore 55030, Pakistan.

We are responsible for (the “controller” of) the personal information described in this policy. In this policy, “we”, “us” and “our” mean Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited, and “you” means anyone who visits our website, contacts us or works with us.

## Information we collect

### Information you give us

- Contact form: your name, email address, company name (optional), the service you are interested in and your project description.

- Ask Kamboh AI: the messages you type and any image you choose to attach. If you ask the assistant to send an inquiry to our team, it also collects the details you provide, such as your name, phone or email, company, the service you need, your timeline and a short project summary, and confirms them with you before sending .

- Email, phone and WhatsApp: the information you share when you contact us directly.

- Client account: if you create an account, your name, email address and password, and optionally your phone number and company. Your password is handled by Google Firebase Authentication; we never see or store it.

- Clients: when you hire us, contract and billing details (such as the signatory's name and role, company details and tax numbers for invoicing) and the project materials you share with us.

Please do not send us sensitive personal information (for example health information, CNIC images, passwords or payment card details) through the website or the AI assistant. Where a service such as SECP registration or tax filing genuinely requires identity documents, we will tell you how to share them securely.

### Information collected automatically

- Server and security logs: our hosting provider automatically records technical information when pages are requested, such as your IP address, browser type, the page requested and the date and time. This is needed to deliver the website and protect it from abuse.

- Spam and abuse protection: to limit automated abuse of the contact form and the AI assistant, our server briefly uses your IP address to count requests. These counters are held only in temporary memory and expire within about an hour.

- Analytics (only with your consent): if you accept analytics cookies, Google Analytics collects information such as the pages you visit, how long you stay, your device and browser type, your approximate location (city or country), how you arrived at our site and whether you submitted the contact form. Google Analytics does not log or store full IP addresses.

- Preferences stored in your browser: your light or dark theme choice and your cookie choice. See our Cookie Policy .

### Information from other sources

If someone refers you to us, or you ask us to review your existing website, app or business, we may look at publicly available information about your business to prepare a better proposal.

## How we use your information

We use personal information only for the purposes below. Where data protection laws such as the EU or UK GDPR apply to you, the table also shows the legal basis we rely on.

Purpose Information used Legal basis (where applicable)

Reply to your inquiry, ask questions and prepare a proposal or quotation Contact details, service, project description Steps taken at your request before entering a contract; our legitimate interest in responding to business inquiries

Deliver our services and manage our relationship with clients Contact, contract and project information Performance of a contract

Invoicing, accounting, tax and company-law records Billing and transaction details Compliance with legal obligations

Provide your client account, show your requests and their status Account and profile details, your inquiries Performance of our agreement with you (the account terms)

Answer questions through Ask Kamboh AI Chat messages and attached images Our legitimate interest in providing instant answers that you choose to request

Keep the website secure and prevent spam, fraud and abuse IP address, technical logs, request counts Our legitimate interest in protecting our website and users

Understand how the website is used and improve it Analytics data Your consent, which you can withdraw at any time

We do not send marketing newsletters unless you ask to receive them, and every such email will include a way to unsubscribe. We do not make decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects on you based solely on automated processing.

## Ask Kamboh AI

Ask Kamboh AI is an AI assistant that answers questions about our services. To generate replies, your messages (and any image you attach) are sent from our server to Google's Gemini API , which processes them under Google's terms for that service.

- Your conversation is kept only in your browser while the page is open. We do not store chat transcripts in our database.

- If you ask the assistant to send an inquiry to our team, the confirmed details are saved as an inquiry and emailed to us, just like a contact form submission.

- If you ask the assistant to fill in the contact form for you, the suggested details are passed to the form through your browser's temporary session storage and removed as soon as the form is filled. Nothing is sent until you press “Send Inquiry”.

- AI answers can be inaccurate. Our team confirms prices, timelines and every other detail before any commitment.

- Please do not share passwords, payment details or sensitive personal information in the chat.

## Client accounts

You can create a free client account to send project requests and follow their status.

- What we store: your name, email address, optional phone number and company, and the dates your account was created and updated. Sign-in is handled by Google Firebase Authentication, which stores your email and a securely hashed password; we never see your password.

- Email verification: we send a verification link to confirm the email address belongs to you. Once verified, your account also shows inquiries you sent earlier from the same email address through our contact form or Ask Kamboh AI.

- What you see: your requests, the service, your description and a simple status (received, in discussion, proposal sent, project started or closed). Our internal notes are never shown.

- Your control: you can update your details or delete your account at any time from the Profile section. Deleting your account permanently removes your sign-in and profile. Requests you already sent are kept as business records under the inquiry retention rule below; email us if you would like them deleted too.

## Cookies and similar technologies

We use a small number of essential browser storage items (for your theme and cookie choice) and, only if you accept them, Google Analytics cookies. We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies. Full details, including names and durations, are in our Cookie Policy .

You can change your choice at any time using “Cookie settings” in the footer of every page.

## Who we share information with

We do not sell or rent personal information. We share it only with trusted service providers who help us run our website and business, under contracts that require them to protect it and use it only on our instructions:

Provider What they do for us Main location

Vercel Inc. Website hosting, content delivery and server logs United States (global network)

Google (Firebase Authentication) Secure sign-in for client accounts and our team United States / Google Cloud regions

Google (Firebase / Cloud Firestore) Secure storage of inquiries and client profiles United States / Google Cloud regions

Google (Gemini API) Generating Ask Kamboh AI replies United States / global

Google (Analytics) Website statistics, only with your consent United States / global

Google (Fonts and Maps) Website fonts on every page, and the office map on the Contact page United States / global

Resend Delivering inquiry emails to our inbox United States

Meta (WhatsApp) Only if you choose to message us on WhatsApp Global

We may also share information with our professional advisers (such as lawyers and accountants) under a duty of confidentiality, with government authorities or courts where the law requires it or to respond to a valid legal request, and with a buyer or successor if our business is ever reorganised or sold, in which case this policy will continue to protect your information.

## International transfers

We are based in Pakistan, and several of our providers process data in the United States and other countries. Where data protection law requires it, we rely on appropriate safeguards for these transfers, such as the standard contractual clauses and data processing terms offered by our providers.

## How long we keep information

- Inquiries that do not become projects: up to 24 months after our last contact with you, so we can follow up on the same conversation, then deleted.

- Client records: for the duration of our relationship and afterwards for as long as company and tax laws require us to keep business and accounting records.

- Analytics data: no longer than 14 months.

- Server logs and abuse counters: for the short periods set by our hosting provider, and about an hour for request counters.

- Client accounts: until you delete your account. We may also delete accounts that have been unused for more than 3 years, after emailing you first.

- Ask Kamboh AI: chat transcripts are not stored by us. Inquiries sent through the assistant follow the inquiry rule above.

## How we protect your information

We use encryption in transit (HTTPS) across the whole website, store inquiries in a database that cannot be accessed directly from the internet, restrict our admin area to named team members who must sign in, and limit access to personal information to people who need it for their work. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, but we work to protect your information and will act promptly if we become aware of a security incident.

## Your rights and choices

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:

- Access the personal information we hold about you and receive a copy

- Correct information that is inaccurate or incomplete

- Delete your information where we no longer need it or you withdraw consent

- Object to or restrict certain uses, including any direct marketing

- Withdraw consent at any time, for example to analytics cookies

- Data portability , receiving your information in a commonly used format

To make a request, email info@kambohtechnologies.com with the subject “Privacy request”. We may need to confirm your identity before acting on it, and we aim to respond within 30 days. You will not be charged for a reasonable request.

If you are in the European Union or United Kingdom, you can also complain to your local data protection authority. If you are in Canada, you can contact the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada. We would appreciate the chance to address your concern first.

## Laws we follow

We handle personal information in line with the laws of Pakistan, including the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (as amended) and the right to privacy protected by Article 14 of the Constitution of Pakistan. Pakistan's proposed personal data protection law has not yet been enacted; when it is, we will update this policy and our practices to comply with it. Where we serve clients or visitors in other countries, we also respect the data protection laws that apply to them, such as the EU and UK GDPR and Canada's PIPEDA.

## Children

Our website and services are intended for businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18. If you believe a child has sent us information, please contact us and we will delete it.

## Links to other websites

Our website links to other sites, such as Google Maps, Instagram, GitHub, WhatsApp and the SECP. We are not responsible for their privacy practices, so please read their policies.

## Changes to this policy

We may update this policy when our services, providers or the law change. The “Last updated” date at the top shows when it was last revised. If we make a significant change, we will make it clear on this page.

## Contact us

# Terms and Conditions

These terms govern your use of kambohtechnologies.com, including Ask Kamboh AI and the information we publish. Please read them carefully. By using the website, you agree to them.

Last updated 4 November 2026 5 min read Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited

In short

- Use the website lawfully and do not try to disrupt, copy or misuse it.

- Our content is general information, not professional legal, tax or financial advice.

- Quotes and AI answers are not binding. Projects are governed by a separate signed agreement.

- These terms are governed by the laws of Pakistan, with the courts at Lahore having jurisdiction.

## About these terms

This website is operated by Kamboh Technologies (Private) Limited (SECP CUIN 0297023), Plot 111, Block A1, PIA Housing Society, Johar Town, Lahore 55030, Pakistan (“we”, “us”, “our”). These terms apply to everyone who visits or uses the website (“you”).

These terms cover use of the website only. When you hire us for a project, that work is governed by a separate written agreement, such as a proposal, statement of work or service agreement, which takes priority over these terms for that project. See our Contract Information page for how our agreements usually work.

## Using our website

You may browse the website, read and share our articles with a link back to the original, and contact us about our services. When you use the website you agree not to:

- Break any law, including the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016, or help anyone else do so

- Try to gain unauthorised access to the website, our admin area, servers or databases, or test their security without our written permission

- Introduce viruses or harmful code, or overload the website with automated requests

- Scrape, copy or republish substantial parts of the website, or use it to train AI models, without our written permission

- Submit false, misleading, offensive or unlawful information through our forms or AI assistant, or impersonate someone else

- Use the contact form or AI assistant to send spam or unsolicited advertising

We may restrict or block access to anyone who breaks these rules.

## Ask Kamboh AI

Ask Kamboh AI is an automated assistant powered by a third-party AI model. It is provided to help you find information quickly, but:

- Its answers are generated automatically and may be incomplete or wrong . They are not offers, quotations, guarantees or professional advice.

- Only a written proposal or agreement from our team is binding on us.

- You must not use the assistant for anything unlawful, to try to make it ignore its instructions, or to obtain information unrelated to our services.

- Your use of the assistant is also covered by our Privacy Policy .

## Client accounts

You can create a free client account to send project requests and follow their status. When you do, you agree to:

- Give accurate details and keep them up to date

- Keep your password secret and tell us straight away if you think someone else has used your account

- Use the account only for genuine requests about our services, and only for yourself or an organisation you are authorised to represent

Sending a request through your account is an inquiry, not a contract. A project only starts when both sides agree a written proposal or agreement. You can delete your account at any time from your account page. We may suspend or delete accounts that break these terms, are used for spam or abuse, or have been unused for a long time.

## Information on this website

We work to keep the website accurate and up to date, but its content, including blog articles and information about SECP registration and tax filing, is general information only . It is not legal, tax, accounting or financial advice and should not be relied on as such. Laws, fees and procedures change; always confirm requirements with the relevant authority or a qualified adviser. See our Disclaimer .

Prices, timelines and service descriptions on the website are indicative. They do not form an offer that you can accept, and we may change them at any time.

## Intellectual property

The website and its content, including text, graphics, designs, illustrations, code, the Kamboh Technologies name and logo, are owned by or licensed to us and are protected by copyright and trademark laws, including the Copyright Ordinance 1962 and the Trade Marks Ordinance 2001 of Pakistan, and international treaties.

You may not use our name, logo or content to suggest that we endorse you or your products. Third-party names and logos shown on the website (for example, technologies we use) belong to their owners and are used only to describe our work.

Ownership of software and designs we create for clients is set out in each client's agreement, not in these terms.

## Submissions and feedback

When you send us an inquiry, you confirm that the information is accurate and that you are allowed to share it. If you send us ideas or feedback about our website or services, we may use them without any obligation to you. We will treat project details you share in confidence as described in our Privacy Policy and, where signed, a non-disclosure agreement.

## Links to other websites

The website contains links to third-party sites and services, such as Google Maps, WhatsApp, Instagram, GitHub and government websites. We do not control them and are not responsible for their content, availability or practices.

## Availability

We aim to keep the website available and secure, but we do not guarantee that it will always be available, uninterrupted or free of errors. We may change, suspend or withdraw any part of it at any time, for example for maintenance.

## Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, the website and its content are provided “as is” and “as available”, without warranties of any kind, express or implied. We are not liable for any indirect, incidental or consequential loss, or for loss of profits, revenue, data or business opportunities, arising from your use of, or inability to use, the website or the AI assistant, or from reliance on any information on it.

Nothing in these terms limits or excludes any liability that cannot be limited or excluded under applicable law, including liability for fraud.

## Indemnity

You agree to compensate us for any claims, losses or costs (including reasonable legal fees) that arise from your misuse of the website or your breach of these terms.

## Electronic communications

When you contact us through the website, by email or by WhatsApp, you agree that we may reply electronically. Under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002, electronic messages, records and signatures can have legal effect, and we accept electronically signed proposals and agreements.

## Governing law and disputes

These terms are governed by the laws of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. We will always try to resolve a concern informally first, so please contact us. If a dispute cannot be resolved, the courts at Lahore, Pakistan will have exclusive jurisdiction, unless the law of your country gives you a right to bring proceedings where you live.
